quarterly_data.signal: Connect 2026 hardware launches (CEO Mark Zuckerberg): Meta VR Glasses, a new VR device in a pair-of-glasses form factor that weighs 'about 100 grams on your face', 'less than one-fifth the weight of Meta Quest 3', enabled by a split architecture, and the first time Meta has 'integrated an AI agent directly into the operating system'; 'We are going to ship it in the spring ... and it is going to cost $1,299.' Muse Charm, a keychain-size handheld that packs 'the whole Muse experience, including the whole real-time voice and avatar stack', is planned 'to have this ready to ship in time for the holidays in December' (only a few built so far; finishing material and component layout still to be finalized). CEO on Reality Labs: 'We made the decision to focus a little bit less on metaverse for now, build fewer VR devices, and only release them when we have real breakthroughs.'
quarterly_data.figure: Meta VR Glasses about 100 grams, $1,299, ship in the spring; Muse Charm planned to ship in December

quarterly_data.signal: AI glasses lineup (CEO Mark Zuckerberg): a new category of audio glasses without cameras, with 'the longest battery of any of our glasses' (a full day of use) and 'the thinnest pair of Ray-Ban Metas that we have ever shipped'; the entire lineup updated with Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 (slimmer frame, adjustable temple tips, Dolby Atmos spatial audio capture, six microphones); new Aviator and Zena models; the style lineup expands to 51 different style combinations, with the Adventurer style 'starting at just $249'; 'by the end of the year, we're going to have more than 100 different styles of glasses available', designed with 'our partners at EssilorLuxottica'. Hearing Enhancement 'turns your glasses into an FDA-cleared, over-the-counter hearing aid' for perceived mild to moderate hearing loss, coming first to Meta Glasses. CEO view: of 'almost 2 billion people in the world who wear glasses today', 'in the coming years, most of these are going to get upgraded to AI glasses'; Meta has 'shifted our focus to building the best devices for personal superintelligence'.
quarterly_data.figure: 51 style combinations; Adventurer from $249; more than 100 styles by the end of the year; six microphones

quarterly_data.signal: Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses (full-color high-resolution display plus the Meta Neural Band, introduced at Connect last year), CEO Mark Zuckerberg: 'They've been in extremely short supply since and sold out for most of the year. But we are finally catching up with demand, so now they're going to be available for sale online at meta.com'; Meta will also, for the first time, 'start rolling them out internationally'.

Muse personal agent (CEO Mark Zuckerberg; Alexander Wang, Meta executive): Muse is 'the personal agent that we shipped a few weeks ago' and is 'already helping millions of people'; every Muse runs on its own Muse secure VM, a Muse confidential VM 'so that even Meta won't be able to see that information' is coming soon, and the Muse Spark model 'is trained specifically to excel as a personal agent'. Business model (CEO): Muse is free 'for a huge number of tokens with the expectation that over time we will profit by taking a small fee from transactions'. Wang: Muse 'just rolled out in Canada, and more countries are coming soon'; the Muse Mac app launched last week and can now drive any app on a Mac; 'Walmart, Best Buy, Gap, Sephora, Wayfair, and many more are integrating with Muse'; the developer Connector Platform 'received over 1,500 applications' in less than a week; 'Pretty soon, we're dropping the most capable model we've ever trained.'
quarterly_data.figure: over 1,500 Connector Platform applications in less than a week; Muse helping millions of people
